A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ARKit LabelMaker and the LabelMakerV2 annotation pipeline. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, references, and appendices support comparison, including content renamed or moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original semantic-segmentation training experiments on ScanNet, ScanNet200, and ScanNet++, plus qualitative results on self-captured scenes.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds annotation-quality evaluations, component ablations, data-scaling experiments, Matterport3D evaluation, and instance-segmentation results.

M1.justification: Grounded-SAM integration, gravity alignment, ensemble voting, point lifting, and mobile-scanner integration already appear in v1. v2's explicit NeuS-omission discussion elaborates the neural-rendering omission already documented in v1 Section 4.6 and Appendix C.1; it does not establish a changed annotation procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds zero-shot semantic evaluation on Matterport3D and instance segmentation on ScanNet and ScanNet200 (Section 4.6, Tables 7–8). These extend both target-domain and task coverage. ScanNet++ remains evaluated in Appendix B, and the self-captured scenes are retained.

E2.justification: v2 adds reported comparisons with LabelMakerV1 and ScanNet's manual annotations in Table 5, and OpenScene and Matterport3D-supervised MinkowskiNet in Table 7. Table 2 also adds a PTv3-PPT ablation comparator. The original MinkowskiNet, PTv3, Mix3D, and PonderV2 comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include label-quality evaluation on five ScanNet and three ARKitScenes scenes, 10/20/50/100% pretraining subsets, size-matched Structured3D, Top-40/80/160 NYU label mappings, accuracy metrics, and instance-segmentation AP metrics. Table 1 also changes the reported ARKit validation/test split from 548/no test set to 274/274, although the caption and prose still state 548 validation scenes.

E4.justification: v2 adds Grounded-SAM/gravity-alignment ablations, direct annotation-quality checks, dataset-size sensitivity and a size-matched synthetic-data comparison (Tables 4–6). New figures analyze gravity-related errors, class frequencies, and individual tail-class detections. The earlier aggregate head/common/tail analysis is retained in the expanded main table.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for benchmark scores. The two Mask3D seeds used for test-time augmentation and the stored vote-count information are documented in both versions; v2 adds no uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Numerous validation scores change: joint PTv3-PPT ScanNet200 mIoU changes from 40.3 to 37.5, while its test score remains 41.4; fine-tuned MinkowskiNet ScanNet20 validation mIoU changes from 77.0 to 74.1. Reasons for these revisions are not stated. v2 adds scaling, annotation-quality, transfer, and instance results, but removes all ScanNet++ test top-1/top-3 scores while retaining its validation scores in Appendix B.

T1.justification: The gravity-alignment mathematical rule is unchanged, and neither version develops formal theorems or proofs. v2's log-linear scaling discussion describes empirical observations rather than a new mathematical derivation or formal result.

C1.justification: The largest-dataset and state-of-the-art segmentation claims remain. v2 recasts the contribution list by explicitly claiming a trade-off analysis of unsupervised, synthetic, and automatically labeled training, replacing the pipeline-improvement bullet. Its highlighted 2.1-point overall and 5.5-point tail-class gains quantify comparisons already present in v1's tables.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations about transferable features, log-linear mIoU scaling despite absent loss scaling, and differing tail-class benefits for PTv3 and MinkowskiNet. It explains NeuS geometry difficulties on inside-out scans. ScanNet++ discussion changes from test deterioration and limited benefits to validation gains qualified by baseline non-reproducibility and unequal training data.

D1.justification: Most preprocessing, hardware, and scheduling details survive in the reorganized appendices. However, v2 removes explicit training-repository links and the DOI from v1 Appendix A, the mobile coordinate/depth-rendering recipe, and the stated PTv3 pretraining learning rate of 0.0016. Project and dataset links remain, and v2 adds an estimated 12 GPU hours per scene for the omitted neural-rendering step.

R1.justification: v2 broadens introductory coverage to distillation, denoising, and additional open-vocabulary approaches, citing works such as OpenScene, OpenNeRF, Search3D, and P2P-Bridge. It also adds references supporting Matterport3D, PointGroup, and NeuS discussions. The central positioning as a LabelMaker extension addressing scarce annotated 3D data remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, methodological explanations, and conclusion receive extensive rewriting. Experiments are reorganized into thematic comparisons, ablations, and transferability sections; ScanNet++ moves to the supplement and references move before it. ALC/ALS200 terminology is replaced with descriptive ARKit LabelMaker names.

P2.justification: v2 adds dataset-size, gravity-alignment, annotation-comparison, class-distribution, tail-detection, and scaling figures, plus several experimental tables. It merges v1 Table 3 and Appendix Table B1 into a wide ScanNet200 table and relocates the ScanNet++ table. Existing pipeline and self-captured-scene figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Tables 4–6 address important gaps in v1 by directly evaluating annotation quality, isolating pipeline components, and testing dataset-size effects against size-matched synthetic data. Transfer experiments further strengthen the evidence for usefulness beyond the original evaluations. These gains substantially improve the paper's empirical foundation, despite removed ScanNet++ test results and reproducibility details, unexplained score revisions, and inconsistent split reporting.
